doc.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Singers: Ella Fitzgerald, Billie Holiday and Sarah Vaughan
summary: He prefers Ella, dislikes singers imitating horns, and says Ella was insecure.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Talk about another vocalist. You worked with Ella Fitzgerald.

Ah! The best. Yeah, they were all good. Billy Holliday of course was an innovator. She influenced so many other singers, but, and Sarah Vaughn was a fantastic musicians, played piano well, but if I had my druthers, it would be Ella.
Do you like playing with vocalists?

I didn’t then. I enjoyed it later on when I could more or less interplay with what they were doing, but I never really leaned towards vocalists, you know, working with them or playing with them. And what I did not like, which Ella could do well by the way, but I did not like most singers who try to emulate the horn and sing bebop, and all that stuff. I never, that wasn’t, it wasn’t real to me, but Ella could do it. Ella could do that. She could actually do almost anything she wanted to do, vocally. Very insecure, too…
Well, her performances, she was never satisfied with her performances. It didn’t matter what the audience thought. They loved her.

And even on a personal level, she was withdrawn a lot and on her own pretty much. And then of course she was swayed by a lot of different men who just seized the opportunity to latch on to somebody famous instead of really taking care of her.
